newsitem.title: FRANCE: Anti-Islamist and bodyguard die in Algerian attack.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Islamist and bodyguard die in Algerian attack.

text.p: Gunmen, thought to be Moslem guerrillas, have shot dead an anti-Islamist activist and his bodyguard at a high school in northern Algeria, political party officials said on Sunday.

The gunmen, disguised as security force members, burst into Ahcene Outaleb high school classroom at Ath Larbaa town in Tizi-Ouzou province, 100 km (62 miles) east of Algiers, killing the anti-Islamist Rally for Culture and Democracy (RCD) party activist, they said.

RCD officials, speaking by telephone from Tizi-Ouzou, said the assailants shot dead Djaffar Ouahioun, a mathematics teacher, in front of his students. The bodyguard, Kamel Ait Hamouda, was also killed in the attack carried out on Saturday, they added.
The killing occurred four days before the start of the Algerian June 5 parliamentary poll campaign. RCD is among 39 political parties competing in the 380-seat National Assembly election.
Several workers from various political parties have been killed in Algeria in the past three years, in attacks the authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas.

About 60,000 people have died in violence between Moslem guerrillas and government forces since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
